title: Accelerating Oncology Drug Discovery via Preprint Synthesis
business: A mid-sized oncology research firm focused on identifying novel protein kinase inhibitors.
problem: Researchers lose weeks manually monitoring hundreds of new biological preprints, leading to delayed identification of emerging therapeutic targets and redundant experimental efforts.
solution: The bioRxiv connector enables Claude to programmatically query the latest preprints, allowing the research team to synthesize findings across multiple biological categories without manual literature review.
steps: Configure the bioRxiv connector within the Claude environment to establish API connectivity.
Define specific search parameters using the search_preprints tool to filter for kinase-related keywords.
Execute automated queries to retrieve metadata and abstracts for papers published within the last 48 hours.
Instruct Claude to summarize the findings and highlight potential conflicts with existing internal research pipelines.
outcome: The research team achieves a more agile R&D cycle by identifying relevant preprints in near real-time, allowing for faster pivot decisions in experimental design.
limitation: The connector accesses preprints that have not yet undergone peer review; users must verify the scientific rigor of findings by checking the get_published_articles tool to see if a peer-reviewed version exists.
